description.narrative:
An “Entrepreneurship Support Programme” was designed in 2020 with ILO’s technical support which includes entrepreneurship trainings, mentorship support on business idea development, financial grant support and follow-up consultancy support to the grantees. The programme targeted Syrian and Turkish entrepreneurs and implemented in collaboration with Mersin Teknopark as the local implementing partner which has recently been nominated as a one of the best national projects to be represented at “European Enterprise Promotion Awards”.
Another enterprise support programme called Worth to Formalize (Kayda Deger) was designed to support formalization of enterprises in 2020. The Kayda Deger aims to support transition of economic units (owned by Syrians under Temporary Protection (SuTP) and the International Protection Status applicants and Holders, IP) functioning informally to formal economy through technical and financial supports. As a response to COVID-19 Pandemic, number of applications to the programme was increased.
Together with the Ministry of Labour and Social Secuirty (MoLSS) ILO initiated a micro finance support programme in 2020 for small businesses owned by refugees (SuTP and IP) and host community members to increase their resilience in the labour market in response to COVID- 19. Total of TRY 11 million is allocated for the use of 2200 refugee and host community member small business owners.
Gender mainstreaming at the enterprise level was supported in 2020 through “Gender Equality Model at Enterprises” programme that aims to promote gender mainstreaming practice at enterprise.
Technical capacities of the refugee and host community member women run cooperatives (Meryem Women’s Cooperative and Cemre Women’s Cooperative) increased by ILO in collaboration with the Ministry of Trade and financial support provided to the cooperatives in 2020 and 2021. Awareness raised on solidarity economy and national regulation. ILO supported the enterprise owners individually to take necessary legal steps for completion of the formalization procedures. Besides, the awareness is raised regarding the advantages and the rights could be hold through formalization through KfW funds.
Regarding the micro finance support programme for small businesses owned by refugees (SuTP and IP) and host community members to increase their resilience in the labour market due to the economic distress caused by COVID- 19; the ILO has put remarkable efforts to increase awareness by advocating the need of micro-finance support for the small businesses. ILOs financial contribution serves to the improved productivity, continuity of the business and working conditions in small businesses.
ILO provided financial and technical contribution to promote sustainability of the refugee and host community women run cooperatives. Both the technical and financial support have been provided by ILO through USBPRM funds. Series of webinars carried out towards cooperative members with participation of the governing and consultancy services provided to COOPs on regulatory frameworks in 2020-21. Implementation agreements were signed with the metropolitan municipalities to increase capacities of COOPs in areas such as product design, business strategy development and fundraising, agriculture, financial literacy, digital marketing, e-commerce, and multimedia production. So far, circa 560 women have benefitted from the ILOs technical and financial support provided to cooperatives in 2020-21.
ILO developed and implemented a tailor made “Gender Equality Model at Enterprises” in 2020 in close collaboration with ILO SCORE team in Colombia aiming to promote gender mainstreaming practice at enterprise. The ILO implemented the model at KARSAN factory in 2020 and 2021. ILO contributed development of gender equality and zero tolerance to violence policy documents through trainings and consultancy services.

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Trade published European Green Deal Action Plan of Turkey in 2021 which covers vide range of areas including green and circular economy, sustainable agriculture and climate action etc. In support of the Government efforts, the green job opportunities have been explored for refugees (Syrian and non-Syrian) and host community members in agriculture. In that regard, in collaboration with the Adana Municipality, ILO supported women members of Meryem Women’s Cooperative through creation of green jobs in agriculture, financial support and vocational training programmes.
As part of increased joint effort with UNDP with reference to ILO-UNDP Global Call for Action, ILO signed a UN to UN Agreement with UNDP to conduct a joint assessment study on the “Employment effects of climate change and green economy policies in Turkey”. ILO provided financial and technical contribution to explore green job opportunities and take attention of the municipalities to green economy as well as recycling services. Alongside with training delivery, the open agricultural was equipped by ILO through USBPRM funds. The Training towards refugees (Syrian –non-Syrian) and host community members were financed by the ILO as well as the consumables to enable the training activities to be run properly and production in 2020 and 2021. In addition to these, the capacity of the cooperative was also supported through the investment made to the cooperative members and to the cooperative itself.
An assessment study to explore opportunities to integrate the promotion of decent work for refugees and host community members in the green economy and agriculture, titled: “Providing Inclusive Employment for Refugees and Host Communities in Turkey through Green Jobs Assessment Report of Potential Pilot Projects in Selected Provinces” has been completed in 2020. Within the scope of the assessment, a review of the current situation of green jobs opportunities in the pilot provinces, international best practices and the identification of potential pilot projects suitable for employment of refugees and vulnerable host community members were identified. The assessment study included stakeholder interviews as well.
ILO and UNDP has initiated joint actions to support private sector and the constituents on business and human rights due diligence in Turkey with a view to develop a joint programme on inclusive and responsible business conduct in Turkey with a focus on human rights and business.
Together with UNDP, ILO supported enterprises through application of a self-assessment tool for businees on human rights due diligence and COVID-19 which wa adopted to Turkey context. The self-assessment tool has a significant emphasis on ILS and ILO Conventions.
